title: [Prototype] Made a Russian Roulette party game over the weekend using AI-generated art – is this fun or nah?
author: Fit_Chemical_8112
selftext:
[Weighted Paws: Chamber Luck](https://ukupnik-io.itch.io/weighted-paws)

https://preview.redd.it/nwyua3gsop5h1.jpg?width=1776&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=75e7ebb35b2e7bf9205f5b5f75f9d0d9c8321933

Spent the weekend throwing together a quick prototype and wanted to get some feedback before going further.

  
The concept: 4 characters take turns in a Russian Roulette-style game. A slot machine rolls to determine how many bullets go into the cylinder. You then decide how to distribute them – and who to shoot. Last one standing wins.

All the art is AI-generated since I'm a solo dev and can't draw to save my life.

I know it's rough around the edges, but I'm curious:

* Does the core loop sound fun / interesting to you?
* Would you actually play something like this?
* Worth developing further or should I move on?

comments.author: Desperate_Prior_5010
comments.body: Surely there are flash games with traditional art and same gameplay already and also there is buckshot roullete if you want something more "complex"

comments.author: matextrem10
comments.body: What did you use for the art? It looks pretty cool!

replies.author: Fit_Chemical_8112
replies.body: I mainly used ChatGPT for generating artwork because it was less restrictive when it came to "violent" scenes. Other models would reject prompts like "Generate damage to the character's head," and similar requests. I used Gemini to help with editing and removing environmental elements such as tables, chairs, and backgrounds. I used Grok to generate videos, which I then turned into sprites for animations.

comments.author: Felfedezni
comments.body: Love it. Worked great on android.
